record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: Construct an integrable supersymmetric extension of the Korteweg-de Vries equation with an odd Poisson structure in which the bosonic evolution equations still couple nontrivially to the fermionic fields, unlike the then-known odd N = 2 example where the bosonic fields do not interact with the fermions in their time evolution.

evidence.quote: A new N = 2 super KdV equation with an odd Poisson structure has been found recently in [7] but the resulting equations are somewhat less interesting in that the bosonic fields do not couple to the fermions in their time evolution. It would be of interest to see whether there are other ‘odd’ integrable extensions displaying fermionic interactions in the bosonic evolution equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The classical Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation $u_t = u_{xxx} + 6 u u_x$ for a single bosonic field $u(x,t)$ admits supersymmetric extensions in which one introduces additional fermionic (Grassmann-odd) fields, and the resulting system is Hamiltonian with respect to some (possibly graded) Poisson bracket on the space of fields. Recall that a Poisson bracket $\{\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\}$ on a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded algebra of functionals is called even if $|\{F,G\}| = |F|+|G| \pmod 2$, and odd if $|\{F,G\}| = |F|+|G|+1 \pmod 2$. An odd Poisson bracket (antibracket) satisfies graded skew-symmetry and a graded Jacobi identity with a shift in parity.
 
There exists an $N=2$ supersymmetric extension of the KdV equation that is Hamiltonian with respect to an odd Poisson structure, but in which the time-evolution equations for the bosonic fields involve only the bosonic fields themselves (the fermionic fields do not appear in the right-hand sides of the bosonic evolution equations).
 
Problem: Construct an integrable supersymmetric extension of the KdV equation, equipped with an odd Poisson (Hamiltonian) structure, such that the system is integrable (admits an infinite hierarchy of commuting conserved quantities or a Lax / bi-Hamiltonian formulation) and such that the time-evolution equations for the bosonic fields depend nontrivially on the fermionic fields. Equivalently, find an "odd" integrable supersymmetric extension of KdV in which the bosonic sector is genuinely coupled to the fermionic sector through the dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned literature on supersymmetric KdV equations and odd Poisson (antibracket) structures, including the N=2 odd super-KdV system noted as having decoupled bosonic dynamics, and various fermionic/supersymmetric extensions of KdV. No source was found that explicitly constructs an integrable odd-Hamiltonian super-KdV extension in which bosons couple nontrivially to fermions, nor a proof that none exists. The status appears unresolved based on the available search evidence.

status_evidence.title: Fermionic extensions of KdV equation
status_evidence.snippet: Only two simple fermionic extensions of the KdV equation pass the Painlevé test: the supersymmetric KdV equation and the super bi-hamiltonian system of Kupershmidt.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of fermionic/supersymmetric extensions of KdV do not identify an integrable odd-Hamiltonian extension with bosons coupled to fermions.

status_evidence.title: N=2 Supercomplexification of the Korteweg-de Vries
status_evidence.snippet: N=2 supercomplexification and supersymmetric extensions of KdV.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study N=2 super-KdV extensions but does not resolve the odd Poisson structure problem with coupled bosonic-fermionic dynamics.

status_evidence.title: On a fermionic extension of K(-1,-2) equation
status_evidence.snippet: Fermionic extension of a KdV-type equation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent papers continue to construct fermionic extensions of KdV-type equations, indicating the topic is still actively studied.
